fields.title: 1. Case ① — NAACP v. X.AI Corp.: Reporting vs. Original Text vs. Filings
fields.md:
| Date (US) | Fact | Source grade · source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-02 | NAACP, 60-day notice of intent to sue | ⑥ (plaintiffs' counsel) [SELC 2026-04-14](https://www.selc.org/press-release/civil-rights-group-sues-xai-for-illegal-pollution-from-data-center-power-plant/) |
| **2026-04-14** | **Lawsuit filed** — plaintiffs NAACP and the NAACP Mississippi State Conference, defendants X.AI Corp. and MZX Tech LLC, U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi. Allegation: **27** gas turbines at the Southaven (Mississippi) power plant operated without an air permit (2025-08 to 12) — supplying power to Colossus 2 (South Memphis). Claims: declaration of violation · halt of unpermitted turbine operation · installation of best available control technology (BACT) · daily fines. Potential emissions (SELC estimate): NOx **over 1,700 tons/year**, particulate matter up to 180 tons, CO up to 500 tons, formaldehyde up to 19 tons | ① (company filing) [10-Q R25 Legal Proceedings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R25.htm), 2026-10-22 · ⑥ [SELC 4/14](https://www.selc.org/press-release/civil-rights-group-sues-xai-for-illegal-pollution-from-data-center-power-plant/) · ⑤ [CNBC 10/31](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/xai-naacp-clean-air-act-lawsuit-dismissal.html) · Complaint [posted by Earthjustice (PDF — body text not read with this round's tools)](https://earthjustice.org/document/naacp-sues-xai-for-clean-air-act-violations-complaint) |
| 2026-05-06 | NAACP **moves for a preliminary injunction** (halt turbine operation) — opposed by SpaceXAI; Mississippi state government files an opposing brief (amicus) | ① [10-Q R25](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R25.htm) |
| 2026-06 | SpaceXAI files a **motion to dismiss** (① turbines are 'nonroad/mobile sources' and exempt from permitting ② NAACP lacks standing ③ citizen-suit provision is unconstitutional). On the 16th of the same month the **Department of Justice (U.S. government) intervenes and moves to dismiss** — "threat to national security, the economy and energy security," with a statement from the Department of Defense CDAO attached. Per NAACP court filings, **57** turbines (up from 27 in February) | ⑤ [CNBC 10/31](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/xai-naacp-clean-air-act-lawsuit-dismissal.html) · ⑥ [Mississippi Free Press 6/16](https://www.mississippifreepress.org/?p=359879) · ⑥ [Earthjustice 10/20](https://earthjustice.org/press/2026/judge-throws-out-u-s-doj-attempt-to-deny-communities-day-in-court-against-musks-company-xai) |
| 2026-10-19 | **Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals**: denies DOJ's motion to stay the district court proceedings (premature). **District court**: allows U.S. government intervention but **does not recognize authority to dismiss** ("cannot unilaterally end a citizen suit") | ① [10-Q R25](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R25.htm) (records appellate denial, permitted intervention, denied dismissal) · ⑥ [Earthjustice 10/20](https://earthjustice.org/press/2026/judge-throws-out-u-s-doj-attempt-to-deny-communities-day-in-court-against-musks-company-xai) · ⑥ [DeSoto County News 10/20](https://desotocountynews.com/mississippi-news/southaven-xai-turbines-lawsuit-proceeds/) |
| **2026-10-30** | **SpaceXAI's motion to dismiss denied** — holdings: ⓐ the power plant (Plant) is not a 'nonroad/mobile source' under federal regulations, so it "was not and is not exempt from permit requirements" ⓑ plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act ⓒ citizen-suit plaintiffs sue "in their own name and for themselves," so this is not an exercise of federal executive power (no violation of Article II or private nondelegation). The court acknowledged that the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) notified in 2025-07 that 'trailer-mounted, under 12 months = mobile/temporary' is exempt, but held that it is not bound by that interpretation. **The merits (whether a violation occurred) and the preliminary injunction are undecided** | ⑥ (plaintiffs) [Earthjustice 10/30](https://earthjustice.org/press/2026/court-denies-xais-motion-to-dismiss-air-pollution-lawsuit-against-elon-musks-company) · [SELC 10/30](https://www.selc.org/press-release/court-tosses-request-to-block-clean-air-act-lawsuit-against-musks-xai/) · ⑤ [CNBC 10/31](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/xai-naacp-clean-air-act-lawsuit-dismissal.html) · ⑥ [TechCrunch 10/31](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/31/judge-allows-naacp-lawsuit-over-xai-data-center-pollution-to-move-forward/) · [The Next Web 11/01](https://thenextweb.com/news/xai-naacp-lawsuit-gas-turbines-motion-to-dismiss-denied/) · Order text [posted by Earthjustice (PDF — body text not read with this round's tools)](https://earthjustice.org/document/xai-denied-motion-to-dismiss-pollution-case) |
| 2026-11-03 | 2 clusters of reports detected (democracy now! etc.) — reprints of the 10/30 ruling above. Detected on **day 4** after the ruling | `data/spacex_watch.json` due |
| Filings | **No SpaceX 8-K or IR** (latest EDGAR 8-K is 10/26, GPU lease). Company position: no response to CNBC and TechCrunch requests for comment. 10-Q litigation reserve **$350M** (2026-09-30, all cases combined — not broken out by case) | ① [EDGAR filing list](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json), retrieved 2026-11-03 · [10-Q R83](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R83.htm) |

**Differences between sources (recorded)**: ⓐ Turbine count — complaint 27 (2026-04) / NAACP June filing 57 / Earthjustice and SELC October materials "dozens" / reporting "at least 35" (citing SELC) — because the timing differs, this is read as a record of expansion, not a contradiction ⓑ Potential emissions — SELC 4/14 'NOx over 1,700 tons/year' vs Earthjustice and SELC October 'NOx 5,000 tons, PM 400 tons, formaldehyde 47 tons exceeded' — appears to be a recalculation due to the increased turbine count, but the original calculation is unverified ⓒ MDEQ permit — DeSoto County News "2026-03 permit for 27 turbines" vs Mississippi Free Press "2026-03 permit for 41 permanent turbines" vs SELC 4/14 "separate 41-unit power plant permit under review" — **MDEQ permit original text unverified**, numbers not adopted ⓓ Case number — complaint header 3:26-cv-00074 (judge initials MPM-JMV) vs judge Debra M. Brown in reporting — reassignment unverified (Sources: table above · [Bloomberg Law 4/14 (search summary)](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/environment-and-energy/naacp-launches-clean-air-lawsuit-over-xai-colossus-data-center)).

**Confirmed as fact (company filing + plaintiffs' announcements + cross-check with top-grade reporting)**: ① The suit was filed on 2026-04-14 and the company disclosed it in its 10-Q ② On 10/19 the DOJ motion to dismiss was denied and intervention allowed; the appellate stay was denied ③ On 10/30 the defendants' motion to dismiss was denied ④ The preliminary injunction is undecided. **Unconfirmed**: full text of the order (PDF not read — holding sentences are quoted from plaintiffs and reporting), the number of turbines covered by the MDEQ permit and its issue date, the number of turbines currently operating, case number and presiding judge (Source: table above).

### 1-1. What this case touches

| Item | Details | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Axis C · C-2027-1 (nameplate 8GW AND AI annual revenue $40 billion) | The Southaven plant is the power source for **Colossus 2**. For the 3Q26 nameplate of 1.7GW to reach 8GW by end-2027, expanding Colossus 2 is the key path (October issue 1-4) — if the preliminary injunction orders a **halt of unpermitted turbine operation**, the nameplate GW path would be affected. However, since there are reports that MDEQ issued a permanent turbine permit in 2026-03 (quantity unverified), **which turbines remain 'unpermitted' is the crux** — no official document | Background record · Kept in progress |
| Axis E | Its definition fits none of the existing E milestones (FAA permit · overseas licensing · collision avoidance · dispute intervention · federal contracts) — data-center environmental regulation is **a kind not in the September issue's Axis E design**. Adding a milestone is for the monthly round (rule: case rounds are incremental) | Registered as open |
| Probability rules R1–R6 | No litigation or environmental regulation in the conditions | Not triggered |
| Financials | The $350M litigation reserve covers all cases combined — cannot be estimated per case. The claimed fine is the per-day cap per violation (reported $124,426/day per violation — complaint text not read) | Numbers not adopted |
| Trigger | Not among existing T1–T8 → **T10 newly created** (Section 5) | New |

(Sources: `state.milestones[C-2027-1]` · [10-Q R83](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R83.htm) · [The Next Web 11/01](https://thenextweb.com/news/xai-naacp-lawsuit-gas-turbines-motion-to-dismiss-denied/) · Section 1 table)

**Record of a monitoring gap in the judgment layer**: The 10-Q (10/22) legal proceedings note (R25) already described this lawsuit along with the preliminary injunction, DOJ intervention and appellate outcome, but the October and November issues **did not open R25** (the open-items list had only 'Item 1A risk factors not read'). The filing had spoken 11 days earlier about a case that news monitoring caught 4 days late — **reading the 10-Q/10-K legal proceedings note** is fixed as a monthly-round preparation item (`open_questions`). Item 1A remains unread (Sources: [10-Q R25](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R25.htm) · `reports/2026-11.md` PHASE 5).
